import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Data provided as a string
data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Set a clean seaborn style for better aesthetics
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create a scatter plot to visualize relationships between key camera features
# X-axis: Megapixels (resolution)
# Y-axis: Price (USD)
# Hue: Brand (distinguish manufacturers by color)
# Size: Weight (grams) - heavier cameras get larger markers
# Style: Sensor Type (different marker shapes for different sensor sizes)
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x="megapixels",
    y="price_usd",
    hue="brand",
    size="weight_grams",
    sizes=(100, 800),  # Adjust marker size range for better visual distinction of weight
    style="sensor_type",
    markers=True,
    palette="viridis",  # Use a perceptually uniform color palette
    s=200 # Default size before 'size' mapping, helps with legend entry size
)

# Add text labels for model year next to each point for additional context
# Also indicate 4K video capability with a small asterisk
for i, row in df.iterrows():
    text_label = f"'{str(row['model_year'])[-2:]}"
    if row['has_video_4k'] == 1:
        text_label += " (4K)"
    plt.text(row['megapixels'] + 0.5, row['price_usd'],
             text_label,
             fontsize=9, ha='left', va='center', color='dimgray')

# Add title and axis labels
plt.title("Camera Price vs. Megapixels by Brand, Weight, and Sensor Type", fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel("Megapixels", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Price (USD)", fontsize=12)

# Adjust legend placement to avoid overlapping with plot elements
# Combine legends for hue, size, and style into a single, well-placed legend
plt.legend(title='Camera Attributes', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Ensure layout is tight to prevent labels/legends from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the plot as a high-resolution PNG file
plt.savefig("output.png", dpi=300)

# Close the plot to free memory
plt.close()
